content.comment_body: Hello, I am seeking advice on connecting a [product_name] module to a variable speed drive over Ethernet. I'm considering a drive with options for interfaces such as Profinet and Ethernet. My goal is to adjust the ramp speed, which appears to require network-based control instead of digital or analog methods. Has anyone tried linking a [product_name] module via Ethernet to a VSD to access parameters or controls, perhaps using Modbus or another protocol? I've read about communication via Profinet, but I'm still unclear about the specifics of the S7 protocol involved.

You haven't specified exactly which [product_name] module you are using, or if you still need to purchase one. The [product_name] Standard supports Ethernet TCP/IP with the S7 protocol. The [product_name] FS4 supports Ethernet TCP/IP with either the S7 protocol or Modbus TCP/IP. I'm not sure which protocol the drive uses. Do you have a link to a manual so we can check the details?

Thank you for your prompt reply. I have a [product_name] FS4. Here is a link to the drive's general information: [url]. The drive offers various connection interfaces—I think I might use the SI-Ethernet interface, but information is limited. I reached out to the manufacturer, who suggested SI-Ethernet could work, but recommended I seek more feedback here as they were not familiar enough with [product_name] modules.

The FS4 supports Modbus TCP/IP, so the SI-Ethernet module may be suitable. [url]. In order to help further, I need to know details such as the relevant Modbus registers, whether the VSD acts as a slave or client, and its Unit-ID. I can help with the [product_name] module side once these points are clarified, but not with the VSD configuration.

It's possible SI-Ethernet can connect with the [product_name] using Modbus TCP/IP, but the drive model isn't shown in the compatibility list. It would be wise to confirm compatibility with the manufacturer before buying. Alternatively, you could consider using an RS485 interface with Modbus RTU and employ a protocol converter to translate RS485 RTU to Ethernet Modbus TCP/IP. Regards, [user_name]
Please refer to the attached PDF document, page 14. This is just an extract, as the full document is too large to upload.

I am familiar with this guide, and have checked the compatibility table as well. Would you prefer to purchase an expansion module without knowing if it's compatible, or ask the manufacturer in advance? Hopefully [user_name] can determine the best course of action.

Thank you to everyone for your assistance. I think the only way forward is to purchase and test the SI-Ethernet option. I plan to use the drive regardless, and if necessary, I can operate it digitally for basic functions or use analog output for speed control. If SI-Ethernet doesn't work out, testing with a PC is still productive, so the investment won't be wasted. I'll return to the forum for more advice on Modbus after I've made the purchase and completed initial configuration.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are working to connect a [product_name] module to a variable speed drive via Ethernet with the goal of controlling parameters such as ramp speed. Key challenges involve protocol compatibility—especially between Modbus TCP/IP and the S7 protocol—and a lack of clear information regarding interface support. There is hesitation to purchase hardware without confirmed compatibility, resulting in users exploring options through trial and error.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to control drive parameters, particularly ramp speed, over Ethernet using the [product_name] module's network features, preferably via Modbus TCP/IP. They expect clear compatibility details and simple configuration steps.
